title: Positive powers preserve a finite family with zero common kernel
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $M$ an $A$-module: an abelian group with scalar multiplication satisfying $1m=m$, $(ab)m=a(bm)$, $(a+b)m=am+bm$ and $a(m+m')=am+am'$. Let $n\geq0$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in A$. Write $M^{\oplus n}$ for the finite direct sum [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. Assume that the additive map $M\to M^{\oplus n}$, $m\mapsto(f_1m,\ldots,f_nm)$, is injective; equivalently, for every $m\in M$, the equations $f_i m=0$ for all $1\leq i\leq n$ imply $m=0$. Then for every tuple of integers $e_1,\ldots,e_n\geq1$ and every $m\in M$, the equations $f_i^{e_i}m=0$ for all $i$ imply $m=0$.

source.place: Algebra Tag 0565 (lemma-when-injective-covering), the induction on the sum of the exponents in the converse proof.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules], the zero tuple is the family all of whose coordinates are zero. Thus injectivity of the displayed additive map gives the hypothesis in the form: if $f_i z=0$ for every $i$, then $z=0$. For $n=0$ the direct sum has just the empty tuple, so injectivity forces $M=0$ and the conclusion holds. Henceforth fix $n>0$ and the scalar family.

source.place: Tag 0565 (lemma-when-injective-covering), converse proof: induction on the sum of the positive exponents.

proof.text: We prove the assertion for all positive exponent tuples and all $z\in M$ by strong induction on the nonnegative integer $s=\sum_{i=1}^n(e_i-1)$. If $s=0$, each summand is nonnegative and hence $e_i=1$ for every $i$. The equations $f_i^{e_i}z=0$ are then $f_i z=0$, so Step 1 gives $z=0$.

source.place: Tag 0565 (lemma-when-injective-covering), converse proof: induction on the sum of the positive exponents.

proof.text: Let $s>0$ and assume the assertion for every tuple whose sum of excess exponents is less than $s$, and for every element of $M$. Choose $k$ with $e_k>1$ and set $z=f_k m$. Define $d_k=e_k-1$ and $d_j=e_j$ for $j\ne k$. All $d_j$ are positive and $\sum_j(d_j-1)=s-1$. For $j=k$, $f_k^{d_k}z=f_k^{e_k}m=0$. For $j\ne k$, commutativity of $A$ and associativity of the action give $f_j^{d_j}z=f_j^{e_j}(f_km)=f_k(f_j^{e_j}m)=0$. The induction hypothesis applied to $(d_j)$ and $z$ therefore gives $f_km=0$.

source.place: Tag 0565 (lemma-when-injective-covering), converse proof: induction on the sum of the positive exponents.

proof.text: Now define $c_k=1$ and $c_j=e_j$ for $j\ne k$. Step 3 gives $f_k^{c_k}m=f_km=0$, and every other equation $f_j^{c_j}m=0$ is an original hypothesis. The tuple is positive and $\sum_j(c_j-1)=s-(e_k-1)<s$. Apply the same strong induction hypothesis to $(c_j)$ and $m$ to obtain $m=0$. This closes the induction and proves the assertion for every positive exponent tuple.

source.place: Tag 0565 (lemma-when-injective-covering), converse proof: induction on the sum of the positive exponents.
